text: 0 = sized to fit the game. Any other value makes every image exactly this size (in GB of 1024 MB); a build fails if the game does not fit.
0 keeps the DLC's own SDK version. 1-11 overrides the SDK major version (and the required firmware).
32 hexadecimal characters used to extract imported DLC packages and for the rebuilt package. Default: 32 zeroes.
32 hexadecimal characters. Development entitlement records are generated for the target Content ID with this key. Default: 32 zeroes.
32 printable ASCII characters written to the project and used by img_verify and img_extract. Debug packages normally use 32 zeros; change it only if you know the package needs another passcode.
A 64 KiB block of a .ffpfsc is stored compressed only if that saves at least this share of it; otherwise it is stored as is, which is faster to read.
A 64 KiB block of a file is stored compressed only if that saves at least this share of it.
A file is stored compressed only if the whole file shrinks by at least this much; 0 keeps every file that shrinks at all.
A folder with your own YouTube app .pkg files (for example v01.000.003 and v01.000.030). The Y2JB tab lists them with the firmware each one is for and installs the right one. Nothing is downloaded.
A game with fakelib/libSceAmpr.sprx needs ampr_emu.index, the list of its files, at its top folder. A new or rebuilt index goes into the image only; the dump folder is never changed.

A smaller image: the game's files go into zstd packs that ampr-emu-ng reads on the console. The bundled runtime goes to fakelib/libSceAmpr.sprx; mount with ShadowMount+ with "Update game fakelib emulators" turned off. Not every game works packed yet: keep your original dump.
A transfer that moves no data for this long fails (and is retried). Raise it for slow USB drives on the console.
Add when the dump has none
Adds a 1 MiB uncompressed placeholder to every chunk that would hold no data. An empty chunk counts as not installed and the console can stall at "Installing... 0 GB".
Adds the index when the dump has none and rebuilds one that no longer matches the game's files, as version 4 did. A game with asset packs keeps its own index.
Adds the index when the dump has none and rebuilds one that no longer matches the game's files. A game with asset packs keeps its own index.
After an .exfat or .ffpkg is converted to .ffpfsc, deletes it — only when full verification passed. Folders are never deleted.
After an image is built and verified, queue its upload to the console's games folder over FTP. Unverified images are never uploaded.
An index the dump already has is copied as it is.
Ask before closing while jobs run
Asks GitHub for the latest release a few seconds after start. Nothing is downloaded or installed without your confirmation, and downloads are checked against the release's SHA-256 list.

Automatic deletes files and replaces files that fit their old space directly in the image, with an undo copy of every changed byte. Other edits write a new image and swap it in after verification. Always rebuild writes a new image for every edit.
Automatic uses the native Oodle encoder when libScePubTools.dll is available, else the built-in one (byte-identical).
Automatic uses the system software the dump requires (param.json). Choose a number to name images for another firmware.
Below-normal CPU priority, low disk priority, three quarters of the cores.
Build a PlayGo layout when the dump has none
Builds PS5 DLC packages on the DLC page.
Builds, verifies and extracts PS5 FPKG packages. You supply your own copy.
Bytes per sector recorded in the image. PS5 loaders expect 512; 4096 only works if the loader is configured for it (for example lvd_exfat_sector_size in ShadowMount's config.ini).
Check for updates when the app starts

Checks sce_sys\trophy2 and sce_sys\uds .ucp archives and packages a corrected copy when their stored SHA-1 digest is stale. A damaged archive stops the build with its name. Off by default: the format is not confirmed on real dumps.
Choose the package size class (attributePub, SDK Fix rule)
Closing stops running jobs and their tools. Their partial output is removed and they can be retried after restart.
Compatible - keep containers, configs and media loose

Compresses each large file of an .ffpfs on its own. Compressed files grow to a whole number of blocks with zero bytes, which some games do not accept; leave this off unless you know the game works with it. .ffpfsc images are always compressed.
Compression level of the DLC data (-4 fastest … 9 smallest).
Compute the SHA-256 of new packages

Contiguous marks every file as one unbroken run of clusters (NoFatChain), as Windows does for files copied onto a fresh volume. FAT chains also records each run in the FAT, for old readers that ignore that flag.
Converter used to rebuild missing or wrongly formatted sce_sys PNG images from their .dds copies. Empty: prospero-dds2png.exe in the toolkit folder, if it is there.
Debug adds tool command lines and timings; use it when reporting a problem.

Declares every PlayGo language in the package (one chunk each, at least 32 chunks) instead of only the game's own list, like the ppr-pkg Companion's option. Used when the package builds its own PlayGo layout.
Declares every empty folder of the dump (outside sce_sys) in the package. DLC emulator mount folders are always declared.
Decrypts and test-decompresses every file of each new package before it is saved. The quick content check always runs.
Delete the game folder after an FFPKG build
Delete the source folder after a verified build
Delete the source folder after an exFAT build
Delete the source image after converting
Deletes the game folder only after a full byte-for-byte verification passed and nothing in it was left out of the image. Structure-only or skipped verification never deletes anything.
Empties versionFileUri in the packaged param.json so the console does not look for official updates of this title.
Every language the stripper removes is first saved here as a verified ZIP, so you can restore it. Must not be inside a game folder.

Everything: every file except executables, modules, sce_sys, sce_module and fakelib (the smallest; ampr-emu-ng serves a fully packed game). Compatible: also keeps root files, containers (.pak, .utoc), configs, media and video folders loose, for games that do not start fully packed.
Executables that start with the PS4 SELF signature get the PS5 signature in a copy used for the package. The dump itself is not changed.
FTP connections used for folder uploads and downloads. More helps with many small files; set 1 if the console's FTP server drops connections.
Faster for games with many small files on SSDs. Leave off for hard disks, where reading the image in order is faster.

Files and folders not packed. A pattern without a slash matches a name anywhere (*.ffpkg); one with a slash matches a path from the dump's top folder (sce_sys/backup). Verification skips them too. By default leftover images from earlier builds are left out.
Files never copied into an image, at any depth. Use * and ? as wildcards, a / to match a path (sce_sys/*.bak), and a trailing / for folders (decrypted/). Verification ignores them too.
Files smaller than this are stored uncompressed.
Fix trophy and UDS archive digests
Folders that hold your PS5 game dumps, one game per sub-folder. The Library scans these. Files in them are only read.

For full packages, sets attributePub from the estimated package size and lowers kernel.addcontMountLevel when the size requires it (the log warns, because separately installed DLC may then not mount). Updates keep their values.
Free space kept in automatically sized images when the option above is Fixed.

Frees space by deleting the dump folder once its image or package passed a full, every-byte verification. Never happens after a structure-only check, a skipped or failed verification, or when the output is inside the source.
Full compares every byte. Structure checks the file list, sizes and the image's own checksums, and is much faster on large games.
Full speed: normal priority and every core.
Hide my user name in problem reports
Higher levels make smaller packs but build much more slowly. The console reads every level at the same speed.
How Dump Rename names game folders when you do not pick a pattern.

How hard builds may use the computer: Low impact keeps it responsive, Maximum is full speed. It sets the cores used (when "CPU threads per job" is 0) and the CPU, disk and memory priority of Sony's publisher and the DLC engine.
How long to wait before a source file that could not be opened is tried again (a virus scanner or another program may hold it for a moment). Raise it for slow network drives.
How long to wait for the PS5 to accept a connection or answer a command.
How many files are written at the same time when extracting several at once. More helps on SSDs with many small files; on a hard drive a low number is faster.
How many more times a source file that cannot be opened (held by antivirus or Windows Search) is tried before the build stops.
How many queue jobs run in parallel. Image builds are limited by the disk, so 1 is usually fastest unless sources and outputs are on different drives.
How many times a job is tried again after it failed because of a read/write error, a tool failure or a timeout. Never retries cancelled jobs, verification failures, missing tools or a full disk.

How much room an automatically sized image keeps free, for files you add later. Standard keeps 1 % of the image, at least 1 GB and at most 8 GB (as before). Fixed makes the smallest image that still has the amount below free.
How the Build page names new images. You can still edit the name for each job.
Inode density (newfs -i). Lower values allow more files per gigabyte; the image grows automatically when a game has more files than the inodes allow.
Jobs refuse to start unless the output drive keeps at least this much free after the build.
Jobs that were waiting when the app closed come back, held until you start the queue. Jobs that were running come back as Interrupted.

Keep both renames the existing file to "name (1).pkg" and saves the new package under the normal name. Overwrite replaces it only after the new package passed its checks; if it does not, the old file is put back and the new package is kept as "name (1).pkg". Stop fails the job before packing starts.
Keep the computer awake while building

Keeps <name>.gp5, <name>.playgo-scenario.json and .gp5-assets\<name>\ next to the package after a successful build. They are always kept after a failure. The build logs are always kept. A project built from an image, or from a folder whose path has non-ASCII characters, names temporary paths and cannot be built again as it is.

Keeps dlc_emu.ini and its fakelib modules and declares its mount folders. Off leaves dlc_emu.ini and the libSceAppContent, libSceNpEntitlementAccess and libSceGameUpdate modules in fakelib out of the package.
Keeps eboot*.bin, param*.sfx, keystone, .prx/.sprx modules, sce_sys and sce_module, .json, .txt and .png files uncompressed so the console can load them directly.
Keeps the PC responsive: idle CPU priority, low disk and memory priority, half the cores.

Keeps the chunks, languages and scenarios of the dump's playgo-chunk.dat, and each file's chunk from playgo-ficm.dat and playgo-hash-table.dat. Off by default: the table format and the path hash are not confirmed on real dumps.
Leaves each job's temporary folder in place for inspection. Folders older than a day are removed at the next start.
Leaves fakelib\ampr_emu.index out of the package. ampr_emu.index in the game's top folder and fakelib\libSceAmpr.sprx are always left out.
Leaves the _DUBLEX_ folder and Unreal Engine "Saved" folders (Engine\Saved, <project>\Saved next to Content\Paks) out of the package.

Leaves the computer on when a job failed, or was cancelled after it had started, so you can see why. A job cancelled while it was still waiting does not count. Off: the action also runs when jobs failed, even all of them.
Logs rotate when they reach the size below.
Lower the required firmware to the game's SDK
Marks the image as case-insensitive, so the console finds DATA.PAK when the game asks for data.pak. Game images need this.
Name shown for the image when it is mounted. Fixed uses the text below (OSFIMG, as earlier versions). Title ID uses the game's ID (PPSA01234) and falls back to the text below.
Never compress executables and system files
Number of chunks of the generated layout. Every chunk is installed before the game starts and every scenario lists every chunk.

Opens every game file once, in parallel, before img_create starts. On Windows this lets antivirus scanning happen in parallel instead of one file at a time inside the Publishing Tools. It changes nothing in the package.
Optional: rebuilds sce_sys images from their .dds copies.
PFS filesystem block size. 64 KiB is what the PS5 uses; smaller blocks waste less space on many small files. Compression always works on 64 KiB units.
PFS only stores folders that contain files. This adds an empty .pfskeep file to each empty folder so it survives; some games (often Unreal Engine) need them. The dump itself is not changed.
PLAINTEXT_NOAUTH (like game packages) or the engine's native encrypted outer layer.

PSVIETHOA's command-line front end of Drakmor's LibProsperoPkg engine, used to build PS5 DLC packages. Choose the .exe or its folder. Empty: the FW_FPKG_CLI environment variable if it is set, otherwise the copy included with a private build.
Passed to img_create as --compression_level. Higher levels make smaller packages and take longer. Tool default passes nothing, which the Publishing Tools treat as level 7.
Port of etaHEN's Direct Package Installer V2 (12800; off by default: set DPI_v2=1 in /data/etaHEN/config.ini), used by Y2JB installs.
Port of the ELF loader for the Payloads page: elfldr 9021 (9020 is the exploit's own loader). 9090 is etaHEN's package installer, not a loader.
Port of the FTP server running on the PS5: ftpsrv 2121, etaHEN 1337, zftpd 2120.
Port of the ShadowMount+ 1.7 HTTP API (10101): version, free space, USB eject and logs. Optional; FTP and the kernel log are used when it does not answer.
Port of the kernel log streamer: klogsrv 3232, etaHEN 9081 (turn on Klog=1). ShadowMount+ "Safe to unplug" watches it.
Port used to send micromount.elf (the ELF loader, usually 9021).
Port used to send shadowmountplus.elf (the ELF loader, usually 9021).

Posts a short summary (how many jobs finished or failed, and their names) to this Discord channel webhook when the queue finishes. Folders are never included, only file names. Leave empty to turn it off. In Discord: channel settings › Integrations › Webhooks › Copy webhook URL.
Prevents sleep (not the screen saver) while any job runs.

Reads each finished image back and compares it with the source; FPKG packages are checked with img_verify instead (Verification > FPKG packages). A job is only reported as done after verification passes.
Reads every pack volume back and checks each chunk (every chunk is also decoded again while it is packed).
Reads the finished package once more and records its SHA-256 in the log and the job details.
Refuse to build an image from a folder without eboot.bin at its top, which is almost always the wrong folder (one level too high or too low).
Removes the source folder once the image is saved, but only when full verification (every byte) passed and the folder contains eboot.bin. Otherwise the folder is kept.
Replaces the dump's own index in the image (legacy Build page behaviour).
Replaces your user folder with ~ in the logs and settings included in a report.
Reuse the dump's PlayGo chunk table
Seconds between a failure and the automatic retry, for example to let a drive or a network share come back.
Seconds to wait, with a Cancel button, before the action above.
Serves zstd-packed games on the console (bundled, GPL-3.0, quer3q/ampr-emu-ng).
Sets attribute3 to 0. This also removes the 120 Hz, VRR and PS5 Pro Enhanced flags, so leave it off unless a game needs it.
ShadowMount+ 1.7 and later need 64 KB, which Automatic always uses. Other sizes are for other loaders; earlier versions of this app picked 32 KB for games with many small files.
Share of the image kept free for the system (newfs -m). 0 uses the whole image, which suits read-only game images; the size of the image does not change.
Shows a Windows notification when the last job finishes while the window is not in front.
Size of each read/write buffer. Larger buffers help on hard disks and network drives; 4 MiB suits most SSDs.
Skip files marked hidden in the source folder. Folders are always copied.
Smallest allocation unit (newfs -f). Smaller fragments waste less space on many small files. A fragment larger than the block size is reduced to the block size.
Sources smaller than this are stored uncompressed inside the .ffpfsc. Game images are far larger, so this rarely matters.
The PC opens the data connections (PASV, then EPSV). Turn off only if the console's FTP server needs active mode; a PC firewall usually blocks that.
The PS5's address on your network (Settings › Network › Connection Status › View Connection Status on the console). Used for FTP, payloads, the kernel log and package installs.
The interface language. Log files and some technical messages stay in English. Translations are machine-made; you can correct them: see the lang folder.
The local ps5_autoloader folder the Autoloader tab edits (autoload.txt and the payloads next to it). Copy the folder to a USB drive or /data on the console yourself; nothing is sent from here.
The package header and the plaintext debug marker are always checked. Format and integrity also runs img_verify with its integrity check, which reads the whole package; Format only skips that read.
The same input always gives the same package bytes.
Threads that compress PFS blocks. 0 uses "CPU threads per job" from Performance. The image is identical whatever the number of threads.
Threads used for compression, hashing and verification. 0 = automatic from the performance mode (Maximum uses every logical core). Lower it to keep the computer responsive while building.
Title ID, title, version and firmware
Tokens: %TITLE% %PPSA% %VERSION% %FIRMWARE% %SDK% %TYPE% %DATE% %FOLDER%. Empty brackets left by a missing value are removed.
UFS2 block size of new .ffpkg images (newfs -b). 64 KB is what PS5 loaders have been fed so far; change it only if a loader asks for something else.
Upload new images to the PS5
Version 2 is the engine's default; version 3 adds shuffles and region hints.
Version written in the image header. Use PS5 for PS5 games.
What the computer does after the last job finishes, whether the jobs succeeded or failed (the switch below can limit that). Nothing happens when every job was cancelled. A countdown lets you cancel.

When DLC is added, look up the game and its regional releases on the PlayStation Store, SerialStation and ProsperoPatches. Only identifiers and game or DLC titles are sent. Off: enter target identifiers manually.
When an image with the same name exists, replace it once the new one is built and verified. The old image is kept until then. Off: the build stops instead.
When an sce_sys PNG is missing or has the wrong colour format (icon0/pic0/pic1 must be RGB, pic2 RGBA), it is rebuilt from the .dds copy with prospero-dds2png.exe.
When requiredSystemSoftwareVersion is higher than the firmware of the game's sdkVersion, it is lowered to that firmware. The Publishing Tools may rewrite this field again.
When the dump has fakelib/libSceAmpr.sprx, its file resolver needs ampr_emu.index at the top folder. The index is added to the image only; the dump is not changed.
When the game uses the AMPR emulator
When the log file reaches this size it is closed and a new one is started.
Where converted DLC packages and updated INIs are saved. Empty: a "DLC packages" folder next to the first input.
Where folder pickers open. Updated automatically.
Where jobs keep intermediate files. Empty: the app's own folder in your local app data. Choose a fast drive with free space.
Where log files are written. Empty: the app's own folder in your local app data.
Where new images and packages go when a job does not name a folder. Empty: next to the source folder.
Where the Library keeps resized cover art (260x390 PNG, a few hundred KB per game). Empty: the app's cache folder in your local app data.
Where uploads go when you do not pick a folder on the console.
Without a usable playgo-chunk.dat: on, the package gets the chunk count below, one small data file per language and the dump's own scenarios; off, a single chunk and a single scenario.
Writes DLC-results-<date>.json and .log into the output folder after each conversion or INI export.
Y2JB update blocking edits app.db and appinfo.db.

Your own copy of the Publishing Tools command-line tool. Choose the .exe, its folder, or a toolkit folder that contains toolchain\ or bin\. The app never includes or downloads Sony software. The SCE_PROSPERO_PUBTOOLS environment variable is used when this is empty.
zlib level for compressed PFS (.ffpfsc and per-file compression). 9 gives the smallest images and is the slowest; 6 is balanced; 1 is fastest with larger output. Every level mounts the same way.
